geometryCheck.method: Shapely covers check against the exact pinned Historical Basemaps GeoJSON bytes and accepted feature indexes.

initialBlind.countScope: Initial blind-review occurrences. Dropped maps the initial unsupported verdicts. Later recovery, narrowing or substantive blockage does not rewrite these original counts.

followUp.countScope: Separate scoped-review occurrences, including rechecks of initial claims; no additional unique-claim total. Dropped maps the three unsupported Xia linkage occurrences.
followUp.note: Eight Almohad and two Chimú occurrences were confirmed. Three Xia historical place-linkage occurrences remained unsupported because the Cambridge table returned 503. The final context omits the linkage; the author-read attribution remains uncertain and blocks the court.

reviewSummary.note: Initial audit preserved: 103 checked, 90 confirmed, one corrected, twelve unsupported mapped to dropped. The separate follow-up checked thirteen occurrences, confirmed ten and left three Xia linkage occurrences unsupported. The controller checked Khmer repository omission and geometry separately. Final research outcomes are three ready courts and two blocked courts. Repeated access failure and bounded absence do not count as confirmation.

publication.note: Research review is complete with three ready courts and two blocked courts. Final controller structural validation passed. Publication remains pending. No game integration is claimed.

a2-west-ans-almohads.locator: Official TEI XML, div2 xml:id d1e10756, The Muwaḥḥid Sect. Count all descendant p elements from 1: paragraphs 12 and 15, rulers 3 and 4; paragraph 16, ruler 5; paragraphs 18 and 20, rulers 7 and 8; paragraph 35, coin legends; paragraphs 42–43, designation, replacement and election; paragraphs 47–48, Muhammad and Yusuf II.
a2-west-ans-almohads.scopedClaim: Hazard identifies ruler 4 as Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yaqub, reigning 595–610 AH/1199–1213 AD, and links him to ruler 3, Abu Yusuf Yaqub. He identifies successor Abu Yaqub Yusuf II as Muhammad's son, reigning 1213–1224. Earlier succession involved replacing a designated son and later caliphal election. Coin legends included the Mahdi and caliphal names and claims. The consulted Abd Allah and Idris ruler entries establish kinship and later reigns but provide no birth date or pre-1200 action.
a2-west-ans-almohads.uncertainty: Earlier successions do not establish a complete rule for 1200. The collateral-household gap is limited to the consulted ruler entries. The Yusuf II passages give no birth date. The source does not explicitly identify manuscript R.33's dedicatee by the combined name Yusuf al-Mustansir. The independent follow-up inspected the official TEI passages and confirmed the scoped claims.
a2-west-ans-almohads.accessNote: The HTTPS ARK XML route redirects to the publisher's HTTP XML route. Fresh requests returned HTTP 200 with 1,870,960 bytes using Python requests timeout=(20,120); readers must allow the public redirect and a 120-second read timeout. The initial independent reader could not inspect the former HTML route.

Bongianino knyter ett manuskript från 599/1203 till ett födelsefirande utan att ange en separat födelsetid. Personen utelämnas tills kronologin kan fastställas. Att identifiera R.33:s mottagare som Yusuf al-Mustansir förblir en osäker slutsats även efter uppföljningen.

people.uncertaintySv: Hon hävdar sina rättigheter som hustru och drottning medan Filip söker skilsmässa. Källan visar ingen vanlig roll som aktiv gemål vid hovet på bokmärkets dag.

people.roleSv: Kungens son, gift med Blanka av Kastilien

birth.noteSv: Källans livsintervall ger födelseåret 1187. Den 1 januari är en spelteknisk dag.

aliveOnBookmark.noteSv: Han föds 1187 och dör 1226 enligt källan.

people.uncertaintySv: Ludvig VIII är det historiska kunganamnet. Han blir kung först 1223 enligt källan; han är kungens son vid bokmärket.

birth.noteSv: Källan anger födelseåret 1188. Den 1 januari är en spelteknisk dag.

aliveOnBookmark.noteSv: Hon föds 1188 och dör 1252 enligt källan.

people.uncertaintySv: Källan daterar giftermålet till 1200. Hennes senare drottningvärdighet, regentskap och barn förs inte tillbaka till bokmärket.

peopleWithheld.reason: Epistolae names her, connects her to Philip and gives her death in 1201. Lex dates his new marriage to 1196. The read passages leave her relationship status after the reconciliation with Ingeborg in September 1200 unresolved, so the roster has no active spouse record for her.

Epistolae states that Agnes bore children but gives no birth dates in the read passage. Lex dates papal legitimation to 1201. The dossier assumes neither a birth before the bookmark nor earlier legal recognition.

searchLog: Opened Treccani Philip II and Louis VIII articles, Met France chronology, Lex/KVINFO Ingeborg, Epistolae Ingeborg and Blanche, Treccani Capetians and the Vatican's Innocent III office table.
Retained four people with lifespan evidence before and after 1200. No source passage fixes their presence at Paris on 31 December 1200.
Kept 1201 legitimation out of 1200 legal status and withheld Agnes's unresolved post-September partnership.
Read Getty Paris through direct requests HTTP 200 after the web tool failed.
The proposed name pool is unbuilt; no generated courtiers or name-pool assets were created.

review.countScope: Initial blind-review occurrences. No additional source-only follow-up occurrence was required for this polity.

polities.blockedReason: No opened institutional or scholarly source identifies a ruler alive and ruling on 1200-12-31. The attested ordinary personal-name pool required for a generated ruler is unavailable. Do not fabricate a person to satisfy the one-ruler template.

titleClaim.noteSv: Kung återger forskarnas benämning på Chimús härskare. Källan belägger inget namngivet ämbetsinnehav år 1200.

polities.successionNoteSv: Forskarna skiljer arvet av kungens ämbete från arvet av hans egendom och gravkult, men belägger ingen regel för vem som skulle efterträda honom år 1200.

successionClaim.noteSv: En senare dynastisk berättelse anger far, son och sonson utan regeringstider. Den visar ingen säker turordning för år 1200. Varken primogenitur eller val efter förmåga får därför historiskt källstöd här.

polities.contextSv: Chan Chan i Mochedalen var Chimús huvudstad. Arkeologer beskriver palats, magasin och gravplattformar där härskarnas hushåll verkade. Källorna ger olika tidsramar för kulturens utveckling och rikets framväxt. De räcker inte för att namnge en härskare eller hans familj den 31 december 1200.

contextClaim.noteSv: UNESCO beskriver samhället under 800- till 1400-talet. D'Altroy placerar framväxten av den makt som blev Chimúriket efter omkring 1200. Ingen av uppgifterna ger ett exakt grundläggningsår eller en daterad hovlista.

seatClaim.noteSv: Getty och UNESCO identifierar Chan Chan som huvudstad. Urban daterar stadens grundläggning till mellan 900 och 1000. Uppgifterna daterar varken en viss härskares hov eller ett bestämt palats till år 1200.

seat.noteSv: Gettys punkt anger en ungefärlig ortsmarkör för lämningarna av Chan Chan. Källorna anger inget namngivet palats för bokmärkets dag.

rulerOnBookmark.noteSv: Ingen granskad källa placerar en identifierad härskare på en bestämd ort den dagen.

coordinateLicense.claimSv: Getty gör TGN:s data tillgängliga enligt ODC-By 1.0.

religion.nameSv: Chimús kult av månen och de döda härskarna
religion.claimSv: Forskarna förknippar Chimús dynastiska tradition med månen och beskriver hur kungens släkt skötte hans kvarlevor efter döden.
religion.noteSv: Uppgifterna gäller breda rekonstruktioner av Chimús traditioner. Källorna belägger ingen namngiven religiös ledare, fast organisation eller viss härskares kultutövning år 1200.

peopleWithheld.reason: The founder belongs to a dynastic legend recorded in 1604. No opened passage places him alive or ruling in 1200; he is also unsuitable as an ordinary generated name.
The dynastic narrative names him as Taycanamo's son but supplies no absolute reign or survival date. Do not assign him to 1200 or recycle his name for a generated ruler.
Campana reproduces this spelling for Guacricaur's son in an undated dynastic sequence. No opened passage anchors him to the bookmark. Later conquests cannot supply an AD 1200 identification.
Voláková places the last independent ruler's defeat in the 1460s, over two centuries after the bookmark. The source does not support his presence in 1200.

namePoolClaim.noteSv: Ingen användbar namnlista för personer omkring år 1200 har sammanställts. Zevallos bok bygger på koloniala handskrifter, men det öppna sammandraget ger ingen användbar lista över vanliga personnamn för år 1200. Moderna namn på byggnader och namn på berömda härskare får inte fylla luckan.

searchLog: Searched Chimú/Chimu, Tacaynamo/Taycanamo, Guacricaur, Nancempinco/Nañcenpinco, 1200, dynastic chronology, Rowe 1948, kingship, succession, moon worship and Chan Chan across institutional and scholarly results.
Reopened UNESCO's Chan Chan record and read Brief synthesis and Authenticity. They give a broad cultural span and a fifteenth-century apogee, with no ruler for 1200.
Opened D'Altroy's Cambridge public Summary. Its political emergence after c. 1200 differs in scope and chronology from earlier broad cultural spans; no annual succession follows.

Downloaded and read Voláková's National Museum paper, printed pp. 57-58, and Campana's university journal article, printed p. 223. Their legendary founder and dynastic sequence do not identify a living ruler at 1200. The final independent king belongs to the fifteenth century.

Searched for Rowe's The Kingdom of Chimor and the anonymous 1604 Trujillo history. Search results led to user-uploaded copies and scholarly discussions. Cited the opened university discussion of the chronicle rather than claiming to have read the original manuscript.

The Met's retired resources PDF URL returned an HTML error. Followed the museum publication page's current download link, downloaded the PDF from the linked CDN, and read printed p. 69 / PDF p. 81 for kingship, court composition and split inheritance.

Opened eHRAF's public abstract for Zuidema's Dynastic structures in Andean culture. It discusses testing dynastic myths and covers 1400-1600; no bookmark ruler emerged. The general Chimu summary did not load its text and direct retrieval returned HTTP 451, so its search snippets were not cited as evidence.

Searched attested ordinary and elite Chimú/Quingnam personal names, Muchik names, colonial genealogies and Zevallos Onomástica Chimú. Direct PUCP origin access returned denial; a reader proxy exposed the public abstract, which mentions Tacaynamo. The abstract supplies no usable ordinary-name list, gender assignments or individual attestations for 1200. Removed the unsupported no-person assertion and unverified full-text-restriction claim.

A Nanzan paper about surviving family names returned HTTP 429/503 and was not cited. Modern or colonial surnames, dynasty names and modern invented building names were not treated as ordinary personal names for 1200. No name pool file or generated person was created.

Reopened Urban's scholarly article as full HTML on SciELO after the former publisher PDF was inaccessible to the initial independent reader. The independent follow-up inspected the introductory settlement chronology and linguistic discussion. Urban attributes the foundation range to Moore and Mackey 2008, p. 783; that underlying work was not inspected.

Fetched Getty TGN 1099735 over HTTPS, read the Coordinates block and capital relationship, and retained decimal coordinates in longitude-latitude order. Independent source review is complete with the substantive ruler/name-pool blocker retained.

reviewCorrections.problem: UNESCO's ninth-to-fifteenth-century wording describes Chimú society's complexity. It does not establish a continuously dated political constitution, a named king in 1200 or imperial control at the later apogee.
reviewCorrections.proposal: Retain the accepted approximate core as a prior map ruling. Limit this source claim to Chan Chan as capital and broad Chimú social complexity; record D'Altroy's later political periodization and the unresolved AD 1200 ruler in the court dossier.

review.countScope: Initial blind-review occurrences; dropped maps the initial unsupported verdict. The separate follow-up confirms Urban's bounded seat/foundation component and the corrected PUCP ordinary-name limitation. Chimú retains its substantive ruler/name-pool blocker.

followUp.countScope: Separate follow-up occurrences, not additional unique initial claims.
